cards.title: Ad Creative Flywheel
cards.summary: Loop UGC sourcing, creator briefing, winner identification, static/AI derivation and in-house production so new creatives feed continuously into the ad account.
cards.use_when: Designing a repeatable monthly creative workflow instead of one-off creative pushes before a launch.

cards.title: In-House and Founder Story Creatives as the Trust Pillar
cards.summary: Keep producing self-made and founder-led video ads because they carry authenticity and brand trust the other two pillars can't, but plan for their limited scalability.
cards.use_when: Allocating production time between team-made content and creator/AI output, or deciding whether to keep running founder-story ads.

cards.title: AI Creatives for Fast, Cheap Angle Testing
cards.summary: Use AI-generated statics and ads to clone proven formats and test new angles in minutes and low cost, then feed winners into the other pillars.
cards.use_when: Rapidly filling gaps in a creative format matrix or testing a batch of new angles before committing creator or in-house production time.

cards.title: Personification: Scaling by Adding New Avatars and Use Cases
cards.summary: Once spend plateaus on one avatar, unlock new audience pockets by creating ads for entirely different buyers and use cases of the same product.
cards.use_when: High-spend accounts (source cites thousands to $10k+/day) that have saturated their primary audience and need a new scaling lever.

cards.title: Awareness-Stage Ad Set Structure: Why It Belongs Inside One Ad Set
cards.summary: Place unaware, problem, solution, product and most-aware creatives in the same ad set to let Meta's algorithm match message to buyer stage rather than forcing manual stage-based targeting.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring ad sets before a launch, or deciding whether to split creative formats across separate audiences.

cards.title: Pillar Speeds: Turnaround Times and Why the Mix Matters
cards.summary: Each creative pillar has a different production speed and control level — AI is minutes/fast, in-house is controlled but capacity-bound, UGC is high-volume but slow to arrive.
cards.use_when: Planning in-app launch dates, accelerating creative testing, or diagnosing why creative supply can't keep up with scale.

cards.title: Why Platform-First Variant Testing Forces a Find-Replace Cycle
cards.summary: Optimising solely on a single winning format creates a dependency on that creative; the source argues this forces endless re-discovery instead of durable scale.
cards.use_when: Reviewing performance data with a plan to trim creatives, or deciding whether to keep spending on non-top-performing ad formats.

cards.title: Ad Creative Funnel Stages with Concrete Format Examples
cards.summary: Use specific creative formats to move buyers from unaware through most-aware, covering education, proof, offers and direct CTAs.
cards.use_when: Writing the creative brief list for a new campaign or filling gaps in an existing funnel format matrix.

cards.title: Evaluating Whether a Creative Portfolio Is Structurally Healthy
cards.summary: Read spend distribution across creatives as the health signal for portfolio-based creative strategy, and correct structure when spend skews to one or two assets.
cards.use_when: Weekly creative review in a scaling ad account to decide whether to cut, keep or add creatives.

cards.title: Use clear product personas and angles as creative targeting hypotheses
cards.summary: The source prioritizes creative relevance over granular audience work; test this emphasis against store results.
cards.use_when: Planning a Meta ad account structure and deciding how much effort to put into interest/lookalike targeting versus creative production.

cards.title: Creative Similarity Score and Its Reach Penalty
cards.summary: Andromeda bundles visually or thematically similar creatives under one entity ID, forcing them to compete for the same audience and inflating frequency while depressing ROAS.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing rising frequency, flat or falling ROAS, and shrinking unique reach across a Meta ad account.

cards.title: Architect Adsets by Concept, Not by Arbitrary Traits
cards.summary: Consolidate creative variations into concept-specific adsets built on Persona plus Angle plus Offer to feed the algorithm clean learning signals.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring Meta ad account adsets before scaling spend.

cards.title: Amount Spent as the Creative Performance Proxy
cards.summary: Because Meta optimizes for multi-click and view-through journeys, amount spent is a more reliable ad-level proxy for creative performance than last-click ROAS.
cards.use_when: Evaluating which top-of-funnel Meta creatives to keep, cut, or scale.

cards.title: Track KPIs at Adset Level to Avoid Last-Click Flaws
cards.summary: Adset-level KPI tracking is more reliable than ad-level for creative decisions because the algorithm optimizes multi-touch paths.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to structure reporting and which creative to cut during active Meta campaigns.

cards.title: Avoid the DPA Death Spiral Masking Weak Prospecting
cards.summary: Dynamic Product Ads can inflate bottom-of-funnel retargeting ROAS while hiding poor top-of-funnel performance.
cards.use_when: Reviewing retargeting or catalog campaigns when overall performance looks strong but new-customer growth is weak.

cards.title: Portfolio Scaling to Avoid Hero-Ad Dependence
cards.summary: Rely on a portfolio of recognizable creative concepts rather than a single hero ad that will hit its spend ceiling and fatigue.
cards.use_when: Scaling Meta spend and deciding whether to concentrate budget on one winner or distribute across a roster.

cards.title: CBO and the 4/64 Pareto Spend Pattern
cards.summary: Campaign Budget Optimization exploits Pareto concentration where roughly 4% of ads command about 64% of spend, but over-concentration creates revenue risk.
cards.use_when: Setting budget distribution rules for Meta campaigns and deciding how much to let the algorithm concentrate spend.

cards.title: Allocate 10-25% of Media Budget to Creative Production
cards.summary: Reserve a meaningful share of media spend for creative production, scaled to the brand's spend level, to sustain the volume needed to combat fatigue.
cards.use_when: Setting the creative production budget for a Meta advertising program.

cards.title: Sequence Ads for Multi-Click and View-Through Journeys
cards.summary: Meta optimizes for multi-touch journeys, so plan ad sequencing and evaluate performance across the journey rather than on isolated clicks.
cards.use_when: Planning ad sequencing and measuring a multi-stage Meta funnel from prospecting to conversion.

cards.title: Creative-as-Targeting: Structuring Meta Ad Sets by Concept
cards.summary: Under Meta's Andromeda system the creative itself does the targeting, so each ad set should hold one concept (persona + angle + offer) rather than a mix.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring Meta ad campaigns and deciding what goes inside each ad set.

cards.title: Diagnose Frequency Above 2 on Cold Ads as a Fatigue Red Flag
cards.summary: Cold-traffic ads should rarely exceed frequency 2; if they do you likely lack creative diversity or volume rather than needing a media-buying fix.
cards.use_when: Weekly or monthly ad account health check, deciding whether to produce more creative or change campaign setup.

cards.title: Creative Portfolio Model: Avoid Over-Levering Into One or Two Ads
cards.summary: Spread spend across many ads rather than one or two heroes, because every creative eventually fatigues and no single ad holds unlimited spend.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much of total spend to concentrate in top-performing ads and whether to keep funding creative production.

cards.title: Use Amount Spent as the Ad-Level Proxy for Creative Performance
cards.summary: At the ad level judge creatives by how much spend Meta allocates to them, because in-platform ROAS at the ad level is distorted by last-click attribution.
cards.use_when: Reviewing the ad-level table in Ads Manager to decide which creatives are working.

cards.title: Measure ROAS at Ad Set and Campaign Level, Not the Ad Level
cards.summary: Reliability of ROAS improves as you move up the account structure from ad to ad set to campaign, so make optimisation decisions higher up.
cards.use_when: Deciding which level of the account to base budget and creative decisions on.

cards.title: The Concept Framework: Persona, Angle, Offer (and Format)
cards.summary: A concept is a persona, an angle, and an offer; changing any one of the three produces genuinely different targeting.
cards.use_when: Ideating the next batch of ads or auditing whether recent ads were actually different from each other.

cards.title: Testing Priority Order: Angle First, Then Offer, Persona, Format
cards.summary: When creative isn't working, fix angle first, then offer, then persona, and test format last.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why ads are underperforming and deciding what variable to test next.

cards.title: Build Sharp Personas From Problems, Not Demographics
cards.summary: Use specific problem-defined archetypes rather than age/gender bands, because broad personas produce forgettable, unscalable creative.
cards.use_when: Writing creative briefs and deciding who each new ad is speaking to.

cards.title: Scale Persona Ideation Manually, Then Use LLMs to Expand
cards.summary: Do 20–40 sharp personas manually first, then use an LLM with heavy context to expand, and curate the output back down.
cards.use_when: Building a persona library for creative ideation.

cards.title: Angle Playbook: Problem Agitation, Contrarian Truth, Curiosity Gap, Proof, Comparison, Transformation
cards.summary: Assemble angles from a known set of persuasive components rather than defaulting to product features.
cards.use_when: Writing ad scripts or deciding what the next angle variant should be.

cards.title: Write Hooks That Call Out a Real Persona With a Real Pain
cards.summary: Hooks drive persona targeting on Meta, so a badly aimed call-out pushes your ad to irrelevant people.
cards.use_when: Producing hooks and opening seconds for video ads.

cards.title: Stop Confusing Creative Activity for Creative Strategy
cards.summary: Launching thousands of ads a month without quality and a point of view wastes budget and signals a misdiagnosed bottleneck.
cards.use_when: Reviewing monthly creative production volume and output quality.

cards.title: Include Creative Production in the Media Budget at 10–25%
cards.summary: The source recommends dedicating roughly 10–25% of media spend to creative production to sustain the volume needed against fatigue.
cards.use_when: Setting or defending the creative production budget for the coming quarter.

cards.title: Do Not Switch Off a Creative That Is Hitting Ad Set KPI
cards.summary: Meta sequences creatives across a purchase journey and optimises on multi-touch, so low ad-level ROAS can be the opener doing the work.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to pause the 'underperforming' ads in a working ad set.

cards.title: Creative Fatigue Is Structural: Build for Obsolescence From Day One
cards.summary: Every creative has a maximum spend ceiling and will fatigue, so plan replacement before decline rather than after.
cards.use_when: Planning the creative roadmap for a scaling account and deciding how far ahead to produce.

cards.title: Format Diversity Is Needed to Reach People Meta Won't Show Certain Formats
cards.summary: Meta suppresses formats a user does not engage with, so a single-format account cannot reach everyone.
cards.use_when: Deciding the format mix for a new batch of ads or auditing why reach has plateaued.

cards.title: Escape Interest Targeting Without Lobbing Everyone Into One Broad Bucket
cards.summary: Broad targeting works because the creative does the targeting, but weak or generic creative then gets pushed to the whole population.
cards.use_when: Setting audience targeting in Meta and writing the call-outs that steer it.

cards.title: Structure Ad Sets by Concept, Not Mixed Formats
cards.summary: Build Meta campaigns with one persona-angle-offer concept per ad set so you get a real learning feedback loop instead of guesswork.
cards.use_when: When structuring a paid social account and deciding what goes in each ad set for a product launch or scaling push.

cards.title: Write the Persona-Angle-Offer Brief Before Any Format
cards.summary: Document a detailed persona, a tailored angle and a value-framed offer as the required foundation before choosing creative formats.
cards.use_when: When briefing new ad creative and deciding what to make, before any format or production decision.

cards.title: Treat the Hook as a Relevancy Promise
cards.summary: The hook's job is to promise relevance to the right viewer, not to trick anyone into watching with bait.
cards.use_when: When scripting or reviewing the first three seconds of any video ad for a product.

cards.title: Allocate Time to More Hooks, Not More Bodies
cards.summary: Spend equal production time producing more hook variations rather than more body variations because the performance delta is larger in hooks.
cards.use_when: When budgeting creative production time for a batch of video ads and deciding how many hooks versus bodies to shoot.

cards.title: Grade a Hook on Five Criteria
cards.summary: Score hooks on clarity, relevance, novelty, specificity and credibility, needing only a few done well rather than all five.
cards.use_when: When reviewing or approving a batch of ad hooks before launching them.

cards.title: Nine Practitioner Hook Types to Deploy on Ecommerce Ads
cards.summary: A menu of hook archetypes to rotate into product ad creative, each with its awareness-stage fit.
cards.use_when: When generating hook concepts for a product's ad batch and needing variety that still converts.

cards.title: Bridge Smoothly from Hook to Body
cards.summary: The transition between hook, body and CTA must blend product introduction, not jump abruptly, or the whole asset fails.
cards.use_when: When scripting the segues in a video ad between the opening, the education and the call to action.

cards.title: Introduce the Product Late in Top-of-Funnel Assets
cards.summary: Delaying product introduction and CTA produces higher-intent, higher-converting viewers even though fewer reach that point.
cards.use_when: When scripting a VSL-style or long-form video ad and deciding where to place the product reveal and CTA.

cards.title: Hook Testing Still Works Post-Andromeda
cards.summary: Test new openings as low-cost refinements of existing product-ad concepts and measure their purchase impact.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to invest in hook variation under Meta's Andromeda-era diversity expectations.

cards.title: Five Questions Before Choosing an Ad Format
cards.summary: Decide format last, after concept, education needs, single-frame communicability, demo needs and awareness stage.
cards.use_when: When selecting whether a concept becomes a static, carousel, UGC video or long-form asset.

cards.title: Use Cost of Production Versus Contribution Margin to Choose Statics or Video
cards.summary: Compare per-ad production cost against expected contribution margin to decide how heavily to invest in statics versus video.
cards.use_when: When budgeting creative production across image and video formats for an ad account.

cards.title: Use Long-Form-Copy Static Ads for Older Audiences
cards.summary: Long-form-copy statics move unaware viewers through awareness stages and reportedly perform well for 50+ audiences.
cards.use_when: When targeting a 50+ demographic on Facebook feeds and creative needs to educate an unaware audience.

cards.title: Build Advertorials With Ranked Lists and a Funnel
cards.summary: An advertorial static driving to a ranked-review article with an only-clickable winner can convert cold traffic via quiz funnel.
cards.use_when: When designing an educational landing funnel that feels like third-party editorial rather than an ad.

cards.title: Use VSSLs for Education-Heavy Products
cards.summary: Video sales letters educate through the full awareness ladder and reportedly pair well with AI-assisted production for cold audiences.
cards.use_when: When a product requires significant education before purchase and you're building a top-of-funnel video asset.

cards.title: Understand Incremental Attribution Before Trusting DPA ROAS
cards.summary: Meta's incremental attribution reveals that DPA ROAS is often much lower on new audiences than the platform default shows.
cards.use_when: When evaluating DPA (dynamic product ad) performance and deciding whether to scale or pull budget.

cards.title: Budget by Creative Volume: 70-90% Top of Funnel
cards.summary: Allocate creative production toward top-of-funnel assets because modern consolidation means budget follows asset volume.
cards.use_when: When deciding how many top- versus bottom-of-funnel assets to produce for an ad account.

cards.title: Run Partnership (Whitelisting) Ads to Borrow Creator Audience Data
cards.summary: Partnership ads run through the creator's profile, using both handles' audience for targeting and feeling more authentic.
cards.use_when: When looking for a scalable, authentic-feeling acquisition ad type that leverages a creator's audience.

cards.title: Size Your Concept Test by Hit Rate
cards.summary: Launch at least 10 ads per new concept and scale volume to your account's actual hit rate to expect a winner.
cards.use_when: When testing a new concept and deciding how many ad variations to produce.

cards.title: Set Minimum Ads per Ad Set and Protect Working Learning Phases
cards.summary: Launch a minimum of three ads per ad set, and only inject new ads into underperforming ad sets, not winners.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to add new ads to an existing ad set or spin up a new one.

cards.title: Don't reset the learning phase on a winning ad set
cards.summary: Protect performing ad sets from new-ad injections that reset sequencing and redistribute spend; only disrupt underperformers.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add new ads into an ad set or campaign that is already hitting your KPI on Meta

cards.title: Amount spent as the top creative performance proxy
cards.summary: Rank creative by amount spent first, then roROAS/CPA, then CPC and CTR, then video hook and hold rates as diagnostics.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a creative report to decide which ads to keep, iterate, scale or kill

cards.title: CBO vs ABO is a risk-tolerance choice
cards.summary: CBO concentrates spend into few ads for higher ROI but more fatigue risk; ABO spreads spend to de-risk and manage product portfolios.
cards.use_when: Choosing campaign budget structure for a store, especially when running multiple products or when efficiency targets change

cards.title: Shift creative mix from desire-led to pain-point-led
cards.summary: Retailers built on campaign shoots skew to desire-led creative; move the mix toward pain-point assets for performance.
cards.use_when: Auditing the creative mix for a fashion, retail or lifestyle store whose account was built from campaign photography

cards.title: Build bottom-of-funnel ads around buyer objections
cards.summary: Map why non-buyers didn't convert by objection type and produce retargeting creative that handles each one.
cards.use_when: Designing retargeting/BOF creative for a store with an established conversion rate

cards.title: Volume beats everything only above a quality bar
cards.summary: Prioritise volume, then concept quality, hook strength, editing, UGC talent and storytelling — but only once each ad clears a minimum quality bar.
cards.use_when: Setting the output target and quality standard for your creative pipeline for a store's paid social programme

cards.title: Two ways to size monthly creative volume
cards.summary: Simple rule: one new ad per $1k monthly spend; better method: back-propagate from new-customer revenue target divided by average expected revenue per ad.
cards.use_when: Setting how many new ads your store needs to produce this month

cards.title: Set creative production budget as a share of media spend by scale
cards.summary: 4–30k/mo spend: founder-led, time not money; 30–100k: ~25% of media budget to production; 100k+: asymptote to ~10%.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much of the paid social budget to allocate to creative production at your current spend level

cards.title: Treat production spend as a revenue driver, not a cost centre
cards.summary: Case example: a 350k/mo brand stuck at 15 ads refused production spend; reworking old winners lifted results, but fatigue eventually reversed them.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to shift a slice of media budget into creative production on a high-spend, low-creative-volume store

cards.title: Test bulk creative and hook variants via Instagram trial reels
cards.summary: Post ads as trial reels with the CTA cut off to read viral reach and retention graphs before spending in Ads Manager.
cards.use_when: Validating a batch of new hooks or rough cuts cheaply before loading them into a paid account

cards.title: Understand total spend capacity and shape the fatigue curve
cards.summary: Every ad has a finite lifetime spend capacity; you can shape the curve to squeeze short-term cash or let high performers breathe longer.
cards.use_when: Deciding how hard to push a winning ad given inventory position, cash conversion cycle and growth rate

cards.title: Diagnose the two causes of creative fatigue
cards.summary: Fatigue comes from the ad itself going stale or from pushing too much spend through too small an audience.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a previously strong ad is losing spend and deciding whether to iterate it or change targeting breadth

cards.title: Four tactical responses once an ad fatigues
cards.summary: Iterate hooks, move to a cost cap campaign, duplicate ad sets (not recommended), port post IDs to a scaling campaign, or rotate formats.
cards.use_when: Choosing what to do with a fatigued ad instead of simply killing it

cards.title: Run media buying as portfolio and inventory management
cards.summary: Above ~50k/month, the media buyer's job is diversifying risk across ads and products and aligning the ad account with commercial objectives, not just maximising profit.
cards.use_when: Reviewing agency or media buyer performance against your actual commercial position (inventory, cash, sell-through)

cards.title: Split production effort across replication, iteration and net-new
cards.summary: Prioritise reproduction of winners most heavily, then iteration on near-misses, then net-new concepts — roughly 50–60/20–30/20–30.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to point your creative team's production hours each month

cards.title: Brief creators properly and vet them via their prior briefs
cards.summary: Creator output quality is a product of your brief quality; vet creators by comparing past work to the brief behind it.
cards.use_when: Sourcing UGC creators or briefing in-house video for a store's ad scripts

cards.title: Where AI helps and hurts in the creative pipeline
cards.summary: Automate briefing/scripting and production heavily with AI, keep human judgement in ideation and analysis.
cards.use_when: Deciding which creative workflow steps to hand to AI for a store's ad production

cards.title: Hire and incentivise a creative strategist
cards.summary: Creative strategy is primarily copywriting; source candidates from copywriters, other brands, or promote designers/editors, and consider a 3%-of-ad-spend variable.
cards.use_when: Building or restructuring the production team behind a store's paid social creative

cards.title: Start organic content before paid for small stores
cards.summary: Organic forces you to learn what content people actually watch, which compounds into paid creative quality.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a small or early-stage store should invest in organic before or alongside Meta spend

cards.title: Meta Creative Team & Production Benchmarks by Monthly Ad Spend
cards.summary: Stage-gated playbook for how many creators, concepts and new assets to run at 4–30k, 30–100k and 100k+ monthly Meta spend.
cards.use_when: You're setting the creative org, output volume and budget split for your store's Meta ad program and need a scale-appropriate structure rather than copying a big brand's setup.

cards.title: Splitting Production Budget Between Iteration and Net-New Concepts
cards.summary: Put most production money into iterating proven creative rather than designing brand-new concepts, because iteration drives the majority of performance.
cards.use_when: You're allocating a paid-social production budget or briefing a creator/editor team on what to make next month.

cards.title: Tracking Cost-per-Asset and Per-Ad ROI to Justify Creative Spend
cards.summary: Build a financial model that tracks cost per creative asset by source and profit contribution per ad, so you can tell whether each content type is worth producing.
cards.use_when: You're deciding whether to keep or cut a creator, agency or content format, or need to defend creative budget to a founder or CFO.

cards.title: Trial Reels and Partnership Ads as Cheap Creative Validation Levers
cards.summary: Use platform-native validation hacks — trial reels at small spend, partnership/whitelisted ads at scaling spend — to de-risk creative before heavy investment.
cards.use_when: You're at the top of a creative testing cycle and want to know which concepts or creator partnerships are worth scaling before committing full budget.

cards.title: Letting Creative Volume, Not Pre-Optimisation, Reveal What Good Looks Like
cards.summary: You cannot know what winning creative looks like in advance — build the volume loop (concepts, scripts, ads in account, feedback) and let the data define good.
cards.use_when: You're tempted to over-plan creative before launching, or you're deciding how much to invest up front in perfecting scripts and concepts.

cards.title: Two-Format Creative System: Top-of-Funnel Problem/Solution and Bottom-of-Funnel Objection Ads
cards.summary: Build only extreme top-of-funnel problem-solution ads and extreme bottom-of-funnel objection ads, letting middle-funnel coverage happen naturally.
cards.use_when: Deciding what creative concepts to brief for a paid social campaign, so you stop wasting production budget on vague middle-funnel ads.
